title: Conjecture 1.5 (Sintiari–Trotignon)
statement_text: (Even hole, diamond, $K_4$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth.
context_text: Sintiari and Trotignon constructed (even hole, pyramid, $K_4$)-free graphs of arbitrarily large treewidth; these graphs contain diamonds, motivating the question of whether excluding diamonds restores bounded treewidth. The present paper's Theorem 1.4 — that (even hole, diamond, pyramid, $K_t$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth for every fixed $t$ — is explicitly identified as a special case of this conjecture.
paper_contribution: Proves Theorem 1.4, that for all $t > 0$ there exists $d_t \geq 0$ such that every (even hole, diamond, pyramid, $K_t$)-free graph has treewidth at most $d_t$, which is a special case of Conjecture 1.5.
paper_title: Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions IV. (Even hole, diamond, pyramid)-free graphs

title: Conjecture 1.6
statement_text: For all $t > 0$ there exists $c_t \geq 0$ such that $\mathrm{tw}(G) \leq c_t$ for every ($C_4$, diamond, theta, prism, even wheel, $K_t$)-free graph $G$.
context_text: $\mathcal{H}$-free means with no induced subgraph isomorphic to a member of $\mathcal{H}$. A hole is an induced cycle of length at least four and $C_4$ is the hole of length four; the diamond is $K_4$ minus an edge. A theta consists of two non-adjacent vertices $a,b$ and three paths of length at least two from $a$ to $b$ whose interiors are pairwise disjoint and anticomplete. A pyramid consists of a vertex $a$, a triangle $b_1b_2b_3$ and three paths $P_i$ from $a$ to $b_i$ such that the sets $P_i\setminus\{a\}$ are pairwise disjoint and anticomplete and at least two $P_i$ have length at least two. A prism consists of two disjoint triangles $a_1a_2a_3$, $b_1b_2b_3$ and three paths $P_i$ from $a_i$ to $b_i$ such that the only edges between distinct $P_i,P_j$ are $a_ia_j$ and $b_ib_j$. A wheel $(H,w)$ is a hole $H$ and a vertex $w$ with at least three pairwise non-adjacent neighbours in $H$; a line wheel is a hole $H$ and a vertex $v\notin H$ whose neighbours in $H$ form two disjoint edges; an even wheel is a line wheel or a wheel $(H,w)$ with $|N(w)\cap H|$ even and $N(w)\cap H$ not a single edge. Thetas, prisms and even wheels contain even holes. The authors prove that ($C_4$, diamond, theta, pyramid, prism, even wheel, $K_t$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth, hence so do (even hole, diamond, pyramid, $K_t$)-free graphs; this is sharp since Sintiari and Trotignon constructed (even hole, pyramid, $K_4$)-free graphs (containing diamonds) of unbounded treewidth. Sintiari and Trotignon conjectured that (even hole, diamond, $K_4$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth; the present conjecture is a slight generalization, obtained by no longer excluding pyramids, and the authors prove many intermediate results in this generality.
paper_title: Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions IV. (Even hole, diamond, pyramid)-free graphs
